# Meet the African startups that raised funding in July 2026
## ORA Technologies
Funding in July 2026: [$2 million Series A extension](https://african-startups.com/news/funding/moroccan-super-app-ora-technologies-raises-2-million-taking-series-a-funding-to-10-million/)

HQ: Morocco

Total funding since inception now sits at nearly $12 million. Azur Innovation Fund led the extension round alongside other Moroccan private investors.

## Built Financial Technologies
Funding in July 2026: [Part of $500k from Village Capital](https://african-startups.com/news/funding/after-rivia-and-vdl-fulfilment-village-capital-invests-500k-in-three-more-ghanaian-startups/)

HQ: Ghana

Founded by Edward Neequaye, it has onboarded more than 18,000 SMEs across Ghana, Kenya, and Nigeria and processed over $1.5 billion in invoices. Total funding to date stands at $365k. Backed through Village Capital’s Africa Ecosystem Catalysts Facility, a $4 million pilot vehicle funded by FMO and the Netherlands Enterprise Agency.

## GrowForMe
Funding in July 2026: [Part of $500k from Village Capital](https://african-startups.com/news/funding/after-rivia-and-vdl-fulfilment-village-capital-invests-500k-in-three-more-ghanaian-startups/)

HQ: Ghana

Earlier backers include Google’s Black Founders Fund, develoPPP Ventures, and the UN Capital Development Fund. Backed through Village Capital’s Africa Ecosystem Catalysts Facility.

## Mathesis Analytics
Funding in July 2026: Undisclosed

HQ: Nigeria

So far, it has helped provide over eight million loans to more than two million borrowers in Nigeria. The company received investment from First Ally Capital to expand its operations across Africa.

## Dimension Data Limited
Funding in July 2026: [$2.9 million](https://african-startups.com/news/funding/nigerias-dimension-data-raises-2-9-million-in-first-tranche-of-14-7-million-bond-programme-to-expand-fibre-infrastructure/)

HQ: Nigeria

## HyperDev
Funding in July 2026: [Over $1 million pre-Seed](https://african-startups.com/news/funding/south-africas-hyperdev-founded-by-ex-openai-and-google-experts-secures-over-1-million-pre-seed-funding/)

HQ: South Africa and Europe

Piotr Sobolewski and Riaz Moola built HyperDev after noticing that existing coding tools helped users start projects but fell apart when it came to actually shipping production-ready software. Less than three months after launch, the platform is approaching 100,000 users across 14 countries. The pre-Seed round was backed by a network of venture capital investors from Europe and the UK, including Loom Ventures.

## Noma Services
Funding in July 2026: [$650k loan](https://african-startups.com/news/funding/nigerian-agribusiness-noma-services-secures-650k-working-capital-and-capex-loan/)

HQ: Abuja, Nigeria

Established in 2018 and incorporated in 2021, the company operates central hubs in Mabushi, Niger, and Kaduna, as well as regional hubs in Kano and Jigawa. Recently, it changed its business model from input financing to direct aggregation, which has gained the attention of its backers.The loan was extended through Sahel Capital’s Social Enterprise Fund for Agriculture in Africa (SEFAA), a fund that provides structured debt to agribusiness SMEs across 13 countries in sub-Saharan Africa.

## BrainsMingle
Funding in July 2026: [$400k Seed](https://african-startups.com/news/funding/brainsmingle-secures-400k-seed-investment-to-scale-its-video-first-professional-networking-platform/)

HQ: Egypt

The Seed round came from BasharSoft Group, Egypt’s largest human capital technology company, which runs WUZZUF and Forasna and serves over nine million users.

Key Takeaways

- Nigeria secured $635M in startup funding so far in 2026 to reclaim the number one position.
- The total funding was led by 4 massive scale-ups contributing 69% of the total startup funding.

## The Heavyweights Driving the Mega-Rounds
Africa: The Big Deal [reported](https://thebigdeal.substack.com/p/q32026c) that Nigerian startups pulled in $635 million through the first three months, taking the top spot.

Investors are definitely writing massive checks, but they are aiming them exclusively at proven scale-ups with serious traction. Four specific companies accounted for 69% of the national total: up $440 million.

You really have to look at the underlying message here. It proves that late-stage growth capital is still very much alive in Africa.

Nigeria Leads African Startup Funding With $635 Million Raised in Nine ...
web.description:
Nigeria has regained its position as Africa’s leading destination for startup investment, attracting $635 million in funding between January and September 2026, according to figures from African investment tracker [Africa: The Big Deal](https://africathebigdeal.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com).

The amount represents a 157% increase from the $247 million raised during the corresponding period in 2025, marking Nigeria’s strongest first-nine-month performance since 2022.

Mobility financing company [Moove](https://www.moove.io/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) led the funding activity with $250 million, followed by payments technology firm [Flutterwave](https://flutterwave.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com), which secured $100 million.

Together, the four companies accounted for $440 million, representing approximately 69% of Nigeria’s total startup funding during the period.

Beyond these major transactions, Nigeria also recorded an increase in the number of startups securing investment. A total of 77 companies raised at least $100,000, compared with 70 during the same period last year.

Nigeria’s performance placed it ahead of Egypt, which attracted $445 million, Kenya with $201 million, and South Africa with $182 million.

Across the continent, startup funding reached approximately $2.16 billion during the nine months, reflecting a slight decline from the previous year.

Transport-focused startups secured $780 million, compared with $760 million raised by fintech companies.

Nigeria’s renewed leadership highlights investor interest in its technology ecosystem.

# Souk raises $1.6m to wake up the inactive 80% of B2B partner programmes with AI
By Isabelle Smurfit

![](https://www.svv.ai/images/news/investmentsouk.webp)

**_Funding round led by SVV with participation from Antler, Fuel Ventures and strategic software angel_** [**_s_**](https://joinsouk.com/)

[Souk](https://joinsouk.com/), the British tech startup building an AI Partner Manager to power go-to-marke [t partn](https://joinsouk.com/) erships, has today announced a $1.6 million pre-seed funding round [.](https://joinsouk.com/)

The round was led by SVV (Sure Valley Ventures), with participation from Antler, Fuel Ventures, and strategic angel investors from across the B2B software industry.

Souk was founded to automate this process and reactivate the dormant 80%.

The fresh capital will be deployed entirely into product development as the team builds out Coco's core architecture.

This funding allows us to focus entirely on product development and deliver an AI-native partner manager that scales seamlessly.”

We couldn't be more excited to lead this round and to support them as they build something genuinely category-defining."

Technical co-founder Ayo is Nigerian and brings deep software engineering expertise.

**About Souk**

Learn more at [joinsouk.com](http://joinsouk.com/).
